correctness.rationale: For each leading-zero group the lexicographic rotation order is exactly descending cyclic following-gap triple; its marked preceding-one rows give the complete adjacency classification even at zero gaps. The gap generating function z^4/((1-z)^2(1-z^3)) counts each six-run circular orientation, with n labeled rotations, while periodic three-equal gaps contribute n/3. The other counts follow from binomial(n,3). The independent direct and grouped implementations compared 8,854 full inputs and 8,435 further ordered gap triples; finite tests corroborate the infinite proof.

value.rationale: Run count governs the most elementary BWT run-length encoding statistic and is relevant to compressed indexing. Weight three is the smallest natural sparse binary layer permitting three different even BWT run counts and maximal six-run separation. The theorem gives all-length sharp frequencies, structural decision criteria, and the almost-sure six-run property among uniform three-one words, substantially beyond a single small numerical example.
